component.name: Radio Noise Key Generator
component.summary: Passwords and keys from RTL-SDR radio noise

description.p: A native GTK4/libadwaita application and command line tool that generates passwords and keys of any length from radio noise picked up by an RTL-SDR dongle — with the entropy measured, not assumed. A small spectrum strip shows the frequency is really empty, one status line shows the live measurements, and a fresh candidate password rotates with every healthy block until you snap it.

Every block of samples must pass the continuous health tests of NIST SP 800-90B (repetition count, adaptive proportion) plus serial and I/Q correlation tests before it is credited with anything, and the credit is the measured min-entropy of that block, halved. Conditioning is SHAKE-256, and 64 bytes from the kernel's getrandom() are mixed into every derivation unconditionally — the output can never be weaker than the kernel's own generator, whatever the dongle hands over. The radio can only add.

The rnkg command line tool drives the same engine for scripts: plain generation, raw key material as hex, capture replay with every measurement reported, and a scriptable snap that rotates candidates until a timer fires or stdin closes.

screenshot.caption: Live rotation on an empty channel, spectrum strip above

description.p: First release: the SP 800-90B health-tested collection engine with per-block measured entropy credit, SHAKE-256 conditioning with the unconditional kernel seed, rejection-sampled alphabets, the GTK window with spectrum strip and live candidate rotation, and the rnkg CLI with capture replay and scriptable snap. Measurements cross-checked against the NIST reference tool on real captures from an RTL-SDR Blog V4.
